extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, and news organizations (Pulitzer Prize entrants and adjudicators)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions and evaluative standards for each Pulitzer Prize journalism category (what kinds of work are eligible and what qualities judges seek). Intended to guide entrants and adjudicators about what constitutes excellence in American journalism across categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Service
rubrics_metrics.description: "For a distinguished example of meritorious public service by a newspaper, magazine or news site through the use of its journalistic resources, including the use of stories, editorials, cartoons, photographs, graphics, videos, databases, multimedia or interactive presentations or other visual material."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often considered the grand prize; awarded as a gold medal. Implicit evaluative dimensions include difficulty, novelty, impact, and public benefit — work should provide meritorious public service using journalistic resources and multiple formats where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For investigative reporting by an individual or team, presented as a single article or series.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires original investigation revealing previously hidden wrongdoing; often holds power accountable. Judges look for originality, depth of investigation, documentation, and public impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For an explanation of complex subjects, demonstrating mastery of the subject, lucid writing, and clear presentation, illuminating significant and complex issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on clarity, subject mastery, and the ability to make complex issues understandable and consequential for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For local reporting that, by its sustained focus on a community, illuminates significant issues, traces underreported topics, or fosters civic dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Values sustained attention to community issues, illuminating underreported topics, and fostering civic engagement and discussion within the locality covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: National Reporting
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates reporting that illuminates issues of national importance, demonstrating breadth, significance, and impact on national discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For coverage of international affairs, including United Nations correspondence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers reporting from abroad that illuminates international issues, conflicts, diplomacy, or global developments with depth and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: For distinguished feature writing giving prime consideration to quality of writing, originality, and concision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges prioritize superior prose craft, original storytelling, and efficient, compelling use of language; human-interest storytelling that reveals larger truths is valued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commentary
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seeks clear, persuasive, and original opinion writing — voice, insight, and ability to illuminate issues through commentary are key.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criticism
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates critical writing (art, culture, criticism) for insight, originality, rigor, and quality of expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: For distinguished editorial writing, the test of excellence being clearness of style, moral purpose, sound reasoning, and power to influence public opinion in what the writer conceives to be the right direction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit evaluative elements: clarity of style, demonstrated moral purpose, logical/sound reasoning, and demonstrable persuasive power to influence public opinion toward the editorial stance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrated Reporting and Commentary
rubrics_metrics.description: For a distinguished example of illustrated reporting and commentary using any medium that combines text and visual storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognizes integrated text-and-visual storytelling across media (illustration, comics, mixed media); judges assess the combination of visual and textual elements and how they together inform and engage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking News Photography
rubrics_metrics.description: For a distinguished example of breaking news photography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates immediacy, news value, visual impact, and the photographer's ability to capture decisive moments under deadline pressure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature Photography
rubrics_metrics.description: For a distinguished example of feature photography.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focuses on storytelling, composition, emotional resonance, and craftsmanship in longer-form or feature-oriented photographic work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audio Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: For a distinguished example of audio journalism that serves the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assesses reporting, storytelling, production quality, and the contribution of audio work to public understanding and interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public benefit / public service
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pulitzer emphasizes public service as a core value (see Public Service category): entries should demonstrate tangible public benefit or service to the community or nation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original investigation / exclusivity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that reveals new information or previously hidden wrongdoing — exclusives or original reporting are specially valued (related to Investigative Reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Holding power accountable
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting that exposes abuses or failures by institutions, officials, or powerful actors and prompts accountability is a central Pulitzer criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illumination of complex subjects
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ability to explain or illuminate complicated topics clearly and accessibly (central to Explanatory Reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustained community focus
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-term attention to local issues that uncovers underreported topics and fosters civic dialogue (key for Local Reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality of writing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Across categories, superior prose craft — clarity, concision, originality, voice — is a recurring standard (especially Feature Writing, Commentary, Criticism, Editorial Writing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Moral purpose
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges look for work motivated by ethical considerations or a clear sense of public good (explicit in Editorial Writing and Public Service).

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence on public opinion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The capacity of work to shape public discussion or opinion is an evaluative factor (noted specifically for Editorial Writing and implied for Public Service/Investigative work).

rubrics_metrics.name: Difficulty of execution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complexity or difficulty involved in producing the work — e.g., investigative obstacles, safety risks, legal challenges, or technical hurdles — is considered in evaluating merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation in presentation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creative or novel use of formats, multimedia, interactive elements, or visual storytelling that enhances public understanding or engagement is rewarded (noted in Public Service and Illustrated Reporting).
